name: EvalForge RAG Starter Benchmark
description: Small illustrative dataset. Review relevance labels before drawing conclusions.

documents.text: RAG combines retrieval with generation. A retriever finds relevant passages from a knowledge source and a language model uses those passages to formulate an answer grounded in evidence.
BM25 is a lexical ranking function based on term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. It is a strong baseline for keyword search.
Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into vectors. Similarity between vectors can retrieve semantically related text even when exact words differ.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines ranked result lists. Each document receives a score based on the reciprocal of a constant plus its rank in each list.
Recall at k measures the fraction of all known relevant documents found within the first k retrieved results.
Precision at k measures how many of the first k results are relevant, divided by k. It penalizes irrelevant documents in the result list.
Mean reciprocal rank averages the reciprocal of the rank of the first relevant result across a set of queries.
Normalized discounted cumulative gain evaluates ranking quality by giving more credit to relevant documents appearing near the top of a ranked list.
A reliable RAG evaluation dataset should include representative queries, document relevance labels, a held-out test set, and documented data provenance.
Latency benchmarking measures retrieval response time. Report measurement environment, warm-up behavior, and median or percentile latency instead of a single run.
An LLM-as-a-judge uses a language model to score answer relevance, groundedness, and correctness against supplied context and evaluation criteria.
Citation accuracy checks whether cited passages support claims in an answer. Groundedness checks whether generated claims are supported by retrieved context.

queries.query: What is retrieval augmented generation and how does it ground answers?
Explain BM25 term frequency and document length normalization.
How can semantic vector search find passages without exact keyword overlap?
How does reciprocal rank fusion combine retrieval rankings?
Define recall at five for search evaluation.
How do we measure the proportion of top results that are relevant?
Which metric rewards the position of the first relevant search result?
How can we evaluate whether relevant passages are ranked near the top?
What makes a reproducible retrieval evaluation dataset?
How should median and percentile response times be reported?
Can an LLM grade relevance and groundedness of a generated answer?
How do you check if answer citations support its claims?
